name: check a written rule by a procedure, not by rereading
one_line: A formal constraint is verified by a mechanical pass over the text, because rereading finds meaning and never finds the breach.
how: When a sheet asks for writing under a rule, print the check beside the rule as a procedure. For a banned letter: one pass with a pencil, circling the letter every time it appears, line by line, and two boxes for how many were found on the first pass and on the second. For a symmetry: number the boxes and print the pairs to compare, 1 against 21, 2 against 20, inward until the two fingers meet. Never print «read it back». A text that reads well is exactly the one whose breach survives a reading. Print the count of what was found rather than a verdict: two on the first pass and none on the second is the record worth keeping, and it is also the only thing that improves.

knobs.effect: Circling suits a ban: one pass, one mark per breach, and the count is the result. Pairing suits a symmetry, where nothing is wrong on its own and only two positions taken together can be.
Two numbers, first pass and second, make the check a measurement that gets better. A tick says the check was done and says nothing at all about what it found.

knobs.knob: whether the difficulty sits on a printed scale
knobs.effect: The Italian letters run E A I O N L R T S C D U from commonest to rarest, from a source crediting Singh and Galli. Printing that row lets the difficulty be chosen; leaving it out means everyone picks Z and nothing happens.

knobs.knob: who wrote the text under the rule
knobs.effect: A hand: the check is real and finds real breaches. A model: the text comes back the right shape with the ban broken, the pencil pass finds it, and an hour has gone on a sheet that should never have been printed.

where_the_work_is: In the procedure being executable without understanding the text. Anybody can circle a letter or compare box 3 with box 19; nobody reliably sees a breach while reading for sense.
breaks: A row of letters and a two-number tally print and scan. On 800x480 the frequency row fits as twelve letters on one line, and the text to be rewritten does not, so a panel carries the setting chosen and the day count and never the task. The move does nothing for composing: eighty-seven words rewritten without a chosen letter have to come from a hand, and the only part safe to print is the ordinary text to start from.
